messages:
alex: Heads-up: AcmeCorp is seeing intermittent 502s from our hosted endpoint when traffic goes through their corporate outbound proxy/load‑balancer chain. They say it began after they flipped on a new edge LB+WAF.

maria: Do we have any sample logs or a repro curl?

alex: From them: '502 gateway error, TLS handshake failed'. They also shared this curl from their proxy node: ```curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood-inference.com' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health -I --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:203.0.113.45``` where 203.0.113.45 is their egress NAT. Response sometimes 200, sometimes 502.

chris: Two quick guesses: 1) their proxy is doing TLS inspection/termination and re‑originating (SNI loss / cert mismatch). 2) their outbound NAT is port‑exhausting and creating short lived connections that our LBs mark unhealthy.

kevin: Also watch for proxy rewriting Host/SNI or adding a client cert. Our health checks expect TLS passthrough to preserve SNI for routing to the right backend. If they terminate TLS and reissue certs we can still serve, but the SNI will be whatever proxy sets. If they set an internal hostname we don't know, LB may fail routing.

alex: They confirmed their proxy terminates TLS and forwards via HTTP/2 to a pool of outbound proxies, then SNAT to internet. They insisted they can't stop TLS inspect.

maria: Ok. Actionable checklist to give them: 
- Allow outbound to our healthcheck hostnames and IP ranges (we provide both but IPs rotate). 
- Ensure proxy preserves SNI/header Host or explicitly rewrite Host to api.redwood-inference.com when forwarding. 
- If using TLS inspection, whitelist our certs or do passthrough for healthcheck paths. 
- Open ephemeral outbound port range (>=1024) — avoid SNAT port exhaustion.

chris: To expand: when SNAT port exhaustion happens you see many connections reused and failures with ECONNRESET / TLS handshake timeouts. Suggest they increase SNAT pool or enable source port preservation if their infra supports it. Also enable keepalives to reduce new connection churn.

kevin: For an immediate short test they can: 
1) Bypass their proxy for a single node and curl directly to confirm host routing: ```curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health``` 
2) From a proxied node, try `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` and compare the certificate CN/SAN returned.

alex: They ran s_client and got our cert intermittently, sometimes their inspection cert appears (CN: corp-inspect.local). When our cert shows up the healthcheck passes.

maria: That strongly implies their WAF is switching modes or sending some requests unchanged. We should give them a minimal allowlist to give to security: 
- egress TCP 443 to api.redwood-inference.com (SNI match) 
- allowlist our LB healthcheck hostnames: `healthcheck.redwood-inference.net` and `hb-backend-redwood.example` (explain they should DNS resolve these; IPs rotate). 
- if they insist on IPs, provide current ephemeral ranges and note they may change: `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/25` (these are example ranges in our doc). Recommend automating DNS lookups rather than static IPs.

chris: Also advise: if their proxy does TLS inspection, configure it to NOT terminate for `*.redwood-inference.com` or at minimum preserve the original SNI header and Host. Many proxies have a bypass list for sensitive upstreams.

kevin: Re: load balancer handoff: our ALB expects client SNI to decide model routing and which backend pool. If SNI is stripped we fallback to default backend which may not have the route and returns 502.

alex: They asked about healthcheck source IPs vs. hostname — they can't allow by hostname in their firewall, only IPs.

maria: If customers must allow IPs, we provide a published list but warn about rotation and recommend they automate a cron that resolves `healthcheck.redwood-inference.net` and updates their firewall. Also allow port 8443 for internal probe if they use internal health ports.

kevin: Example diagnostic command to script: ```dig +short healthcheck.redwood-inference.net | sort -u``` then compare with firewall rules. Share this snippet with them.

chris: One more gotcha: some enterprise LBs do connection pooling to upstreams and reuse the same connection for multiple client sessions. If the upstream keeps state based on X‑Forwarded‑For or TLS session, that pooling can confuse health/stateful routing. Recommend disabling aggressive upstream pooling for the path to api.redwood-inference.com/v1/* while debugging.

alex: I'll send AcmeCorp a short doc with: allowlist + DNS automation snippet + quick tests (curl, s_client) + suggestion to increase SNAT pool / keepalives / bypass TLS inspect for our hostnames.

ops-bot: Automated note: ticket #INC-5421 created for AcmeCorp networking escalation. SLA 3 business days.

maria: Thanks Alex — can you paste the exact IP ranges you'll share so I can put them in the KB?

alex: Current published ranges (subject to change): `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/25`, `192.0.2.128/26`. I'll flag ops to generate a monthly export so customers can subscribe to updates.

kevin: I'll add a short blurb to our KB about 'When TLS inspect breaks SNI-based routing' that includes sample openssl and curl checks.

chris: Follow-up: if they can't change the proxy, we can offer them Dedicated (private egress) so traffic comes from a predictable set of IPs under a contract. Worth mentioning as a remediation for large customers.

alex: AcmeCorp replied after testing: 'bypassing TLS inspect for api.redwood-inference.com fixed the failures' — marking this as resolved for now. I'll keep the ticket open until they automate DNS updates. :thumbsup:
